title: Custom and error middleware
idea: Error-handling middleware takes four arguments. Calling `next(err)` skips every normal middleware and lands there; a middleware factory returns a configured middleware.

analogy.text: A factory line with an emergency chute. A faulty part drops down the chute past every station, straight to the repair desk.
analogy.breaks: The repair desk can still send a normal reply to the client.

points: `next(err)` skips normal middleware and runs the next one with four arguments.
In Express 5, a rejected promise from an async handler calls `next(err)` for you.
A factory such as `requireRole('admin')` returns a middleware that remembers `'admin'`.
Order matters: register error handlers last, after every route.

code.caption: Edit it: add `requireRole('viewer')` and test a viewer. Each result remembers its own role.

pitfalls: Declare error handlers last; one placed before the routes never sees their errors.
Keep all four parameters, even unused ones, or Express treats it as normal middleware.
Never send `err.stack` or raw internal messages to the client.

quiz.why: Each call to the factory closes over its own `role`. isAdmin wants admin, isEditor wants editor.

takeaway: Errors skip ahead to the four-argument handler; factories bake in settings.
